reply:
Let’s continue with the two sentence prefixes:

• “She deposited cash at the bank”
• “They pulled the canoe onto the bank”

Assume the tokenizer gives the final “bank” the same vocabulary token in both. Its token ID stays the same because that ID identifies a vocabulary entry, regardless of the sentence.

The contextual representation is computed by processing that token together with the preceding words. “Deposited cash” and “pulled the canoe” supply different information, so the computed representation can differ even though the ID is unchanged.

This matters for what comes next: the model can use those different representations to make different next-token predictions. A fixed token identity therefore doesn’t force the model to treat every occurrence alike.
